strategies.name: vwap_trend_continuation_retest
strategies.entry_summary: In a directional session where the trader already has a long or short idea, wait for price to extend away from VWAP into at least the first, preferably the second, standard-deviation band, then enter in the trend direction after price breaks back through and retests that band/level. strategies.name: vwap_band_mean_reversion
strategies.entry_summary: Use the outer VWAP standard-deviation bands as overbought/oversold areas for reversal trades: look for a trade when price reaches the lower or upper extreme bands, betting on rebalancing back toward fair value. The setup is framed as buying lower-band extremes or selling upper-band extremes.
strategies.exit_summary: Target the central VWAP as the rebalancing destination for price.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter at or near lower standard-deviation extremes as the most convenient price of the session
variants.transcript_quote: if you're using reversal strategies you might want to use these as some sort of overbought or oversold levels... and use the central vwap as a target

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter at or near upper standard-deviation extremes as overbought relative to session volume
variants.transcript_quote: the more we trade in the outer bands the higher is the probability that at least we are going going to see a bounce back to the fair value

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches two opposed executable skeletons: trend-continuation after a reclaim/retest from VWAP band extremes, and mean-reversion from outer VWAP bands back to central VWAP; they share VWAP levels but Rule 2 requires splitting opposites.
